items.title: Joan of Arc was burned at Rouen in 1431, aged 19
items.claim: What did Joan of Arc achieve before her execution?

options.text: Nothing — her story is later legend

She convinced Charles VII she had divine guidance, led French forces to relieve the siege of Orléans in May 1429, helped recover Reims and have Charles crowned (July 1429); captured by Burgundians, sold to the English, tried for heresy and burned at Rouen on 30 May 1431
She was a Burgundian general who switched sides
She was canonised within months of her death

items.reveal:
Joan was a peasant from Domrémy who claimed visions of St Michael, St Catherine and St Margaret from age 13. After persuading Charles's court at Chinon, she joined the relief of Orléans aged 17. The siege was lifted in nine days; Reims (the traditional coronation city) was retaken; Charles VII was crowned on 17 July 1429.

She was captured at Compiègne (May 1430), held for ransom by the Burgundians, sold to the English, and tried by a French ecclesiastical court at Rouen. The trial of 1455-56 (after the English left) annulled the conviction. She was canonised in 1920.

The Hundred Years War ended in French victory at Castillon (1453).
items.why: The Hundred Years War's turning point is a teenager with no military training. Joan of Arc's trial transcripts survive — she remains one of the most documented medieval figures and a case in how religion, war and gender intersect.

items.title: The First Crusade captured Jerusalem with massacre in 1099
items.claim: What happened when the First Crusade took Jerusalem?

options.text: On 15 July 1099 crusaders breached the walls; over the following days a massacre of Muslim and Jewish inhabitants followed — chroniclers (including Raymond of Aguilers) recorded slaughter so extensive that 'one waded in blood up to the ankles'

items.reveal:
The crusade had left Europe in 1096. After taking Antioch (1098), the army of around 14,000 reached Jerusalem in June 1099. The walls were breached on 15 July; the massacre that followed killed thousands. Jewish inhabitants who took refuge in a synagogue were burned alive.

Godfrey of Bouillon was elected 'Defender of the Holy Sepulchre' (refusing the title of king); his brother Baldwin became Baldwin I of Jerusalem in 1100. The Kingdom of Jerusalem lasted until 1291 (fall of Acre).

Saladin recaptured Jerusalem in 1187 with notably less violence — he allowed inhabitants to ransom themselves and many to leave safely, in deliberate contrast to 1099.
items.why: Religious warfare in the high Middle Ages was often atrocious. The 1099 massacre shaped Muslim-Christian relations for centuries — and the comparison with Saladin's 1187 conduct is one that Muslim sources have made repeatedly.

items.title: The Korean War never formally ended
items.claim: How did the Korean War conclude?

options.text: An armistice signed at Panmunjom on 27 July 1953 by representatives of the UN Command, North Korea and China — but no peace treaty; the Koreas remain technically at war and the DMZ at the 38th parallel divides them

items.reveal:
Armistice negotiations began in July 1951 and lasted two years, largely over the issue of prisoner repatriation. South Korean President Syngman Rhee refused to sign and unilaterally released 27,000 North Korean POWs in June 1953.

The Korean Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) is 4 km wide and around 250 km long — one of the most heavily militarised borders in the world. Periodic incidents (the 1968 capture of USS Pueblo, the 2010 Yeonpyeong shelling) keep the conflict warm.

Moves toward a formal peace declaration have repeatedly stalled. The Korean War cost around 3 million lives — Korean civilians the majority — and shaped East Asian security for over 70 years.
items.why: Unresolved conflicts shape decades. The absence of a Korean peace treaty in 1953 is the structural foundation of every subsequent crisis on the peninsula.
